name: Cinder Lake Crater Field
coord_source: USGS GNIS feature id 27656 'Cinder Lake' (Flat, Coconino County, AZ; quad Sunset Crater West)
reason: Craters blasted by USGS/NASA in July and October 1967 (47 then 96 more, 143 total) expressly to replicate the lunar surface for Apollo training. Crater Field #1 was designed to duplicate an area within Mare Tranquillitatis, from a Lunar Orbiter image of the Apollo 11 landing site.
citation: USGS Astrogeology, Flagstaff; USGS data release doi:10.5066/P13W5FTZ
notes: GNIS returned exactly ONE feature matching 'Cinder Lake' in Arizona, so there was no choice to make. THE ONLY SITE IN THIS LIST BUILT RATHER THAN FOUND: selected for logistics (proximity to USGS Astrogeology in Flagstaff), not for climate or terrain similarity.

notes: Cross-checked against USGS AnalogSites 'Barringer (= Meteor)' at 35.0333,-111.0170: 0.8 km apart.

reason: NASA lunar rover field tests; source of lunar regolith simulant.
citation: Pacific International Space Center for Exploration Systems (PISCES), Hawaii

name: Moses Lake dune field
coord_source: USGS GNIS feature id 1514643 'No-Outlet Sand Hills' (Area, Grant County, WA; quad Moses Lake South)
reason: NASA lunar rover mobility testing in the sand dunes.
citation: NASA lunar rover mobility field tests, Moses Lake, Washington
notes: NAME DISCREPANCY RECORDED: GNIS has no feature called 'Moses Lake Sand Dunes'. Of the 6 GNIS features named 'Moses Lake' (reservoir, populated place, civil division, historical airfield, CDP, city) NONE is a dune field. This row takes 'No-Outlet Sand Hills', the only Grant County sand feature of class Area, on the Moses Lake South quad, 10.5 km south of the city centre -- consistent with the dunes lying south of town. The identification is by location and class, not by name, so treat it as probable rather than certain. v1 of this file used the CITY coordinate and was marked unverified.

name: Black Point Lava Flow
coord_source: USGS GNIS feature id 1577 'Black Point' (Bench, Coconino County, AZ; quad Wupatki NE)
reason: NASA Desert RATS (Research and Technology Studies) analog field campaigns.
notes: GNIS returned 5 Arizona features matching 'Black Point': this one (Bench, Coconino, quad Wupatki NE); 'Black Point' summit in Graham County (33.1070,-110.0820); 'Black Point Reservoir' in Mohave (36.6499,-113.0415); 'Black Point Tank' in Graham (33.0056,-109.7477); and 'Black Point' cliff in Pinal (33.3217,-111.3201). TAKEN: the Coconino County feature, because the Desert RATS site is the basalt flow near Wupatki north-east of Flagstaff and the other four are in southern or western Arizona. GNIS names the POINT, not the flow, so this is the landform's reference point rather than the flow's centroid.
